Summary and FSR-informed interpretation:
- Policy stance: The FOMC held the target range at 5.25–5.50% and continued balance sheet runoff (Treasuries capped at $60B/month; agency MBS at $35B), operating in the ample-reserves framework with IORB at 5.4% and ON RRP at 5.3%. Cuts are contingent on “greater confidence” that inflation is sustainably moving to 2%.
- Macro tone: Solid real activity and strong labor markets alongside easing—but still-elevated—inflation. The Committee sees risks to employment and inflation goals moving toward better balance, but remains highly attentive to inflation.
- Financial Stability Report lens: The FSR highlights persistent vulnerabilities that argue for caution even as macro data improve:
  • Funding risks remain in money market funds (including tax‑exempt MMFs), and an ample-floor system relies on market functioning under rate volatility. 
  • Treasury market structure shows leveraged hedge fund activity (for example, basis trades) amid elevated rate volatility; this can amplify stress.
  • Commercial real estate—especially offices with high vacancy rates—continues to pressure credit quality, with banks and securitizations exposed.
  • Elevated public debt, geopolitics, and external growth risks (for example, China weakness) could tighten financial conditions abruptly.
  • Corporate credit shows higher shares of BBB and high-yield exposures; default risk is still a watchpoint even if near-term performance is stable.
- Implication: The FSR’s vulnerabilities temper the otherwise “better balance” narrative, reinforcing a cautiously hawkish stance and the Fed’s emphasis on disinflation credibility and stable market functioning.

Net tone: cautiously hawkish with incremental caution from the FSR’s vulnerabilities.
